rationale: Table1.tex row 'Employment elasticity w.r.t. MW', column (1) reports exactly 0.024 with clustered std. err. (0.025) (tables/tables/Table1.tex lines 13-14). This is byte-for-byte identical to the paper value of 0.024 (std. err. 0.025), well within ±1σ. The supporting rows confirm the construction: the elasticity is (Δa + Δb)/%ΔMW = (0.021 - 0.018)/0.101 ≈ 0.024 (lines 3,5,19), and %ΔMW ≈ 0.101 matches the stated ~10.1%. The implied t-statistic (0.024/0.025 ≈ 0.96) confirms statistical insignificance, and the estimate is far from Meer and West's -0.074, consistent with ruling out substantial aggregate employment reductions. fix_severity.json notes the estimation was ported from Stata to R/fixest (major, environment-driven) but the exact reproduction of the point estimate and SE indicates the port faithfully replicated the fixed-effects absorption, weighting, and clustering.
